potential_dependency_factors.rule: author identity may correlate with some style/craft choices but cannot be assumed to dominate every narrative dimension
shared canon/world/characters can correlate observations, while cross-volume change can itself be valuable within-series evidence
genre conventions can explain apparent common mechanisms or expose transfer boundaries
serialization venue, reader expectations and publication model can alter acquisition/pacing without determining all literary dimensions
historical period can affect language, institutions, audience and narrative convention
translated surface prose is not clean evidence of original author stylometry; story/discourse evidence may remain usable with care
shared POV/focalization can create similar information architecture independent of author
short novel, epic series and web serial impose different structural/page-cost pressures
topic/setting can contaminate lexical/style comparisons and some worldbuilding observations
edition, translator and editorial intervention can affect surface/style evidence
successful/canonical works create survivorship bias and are not automatically causal examples

comparison_designs.value: holds author partly constant while varying work/topic/structure; useful for detecting within-author variation and challenging author-essentialist claims
holds much canon/context constant while observing engine, character, discourse and pacing change across volumes/arcs
reduces genre mismatch while testing whether a mechanism survives author change
tests whether a functional mechanism transfers when surface genre changes
tests whether a claimed mechanism actually varies inside one work
same-looking trope/device but different narrative function; useful against surface imitation
different trope/device producing similar reader/story function; useful for extracting transferable mechanism
